patterns.name: factory
patterns.title: Typed Factory
patterns.intent: Construct one of several product types from a key, with the key narrowing the return type at compile time and untrusted keys handled at the boundary.

options.name: registration
options.description: Whether the set of kinds is closed. `static` fixes it at construction, which is the whole compile-time benefit. `dynamic` adds `extend`, returning a new factory whose type is widened by the creators added, so a plugin discovered at run time is still typed.

options.name: errorMode
options.description: How `from` reports a key it does not recognise. `result` returns a value carrying the unknown key and the ones it knows; `throw` raises an error carrying the same. Only `from` can fail — `create` takes a key the compiler has already checked.

options.name: context
options.description: Pass a shared context to every creator alongside the input, so creators can reach dependencies without closing over module state.

options.name: includeTests
options.description: Emit an executable test suite alongside the implementation.

patterns.provenance: Original implementation. The factory idea is the Gang of Four's "Design Patterns" (1994), but nothing here is adapted from it: the book's formulation is a class hierarchy with a virtual constructor, and this is a key-indexed product map whose lookup narrows the return type, which is a TypeScript type-system construction with no equivalent in the original.
